Since you're a hunter I would suggest trying the radar, this alone will help you a lot with anticipating enemies that are about to turn a corner or enemies that are about to flank you while you're aiming. I'm a hunter main and this is the only exotic I use in pvp and has served me well in getting the rewards.

Getting the void points for the weapon I would suggest using the handcannon in comp. It's the fastest way to get your points and it's a very consistent weapon to get kills with.

Don't use that weapon, the time to kill on that weapon is horrendous which is why you never see anyone use it anymore. 

The state the game is in right now on consoles only the fast handcannons are worth using, even once you unlock the other weapons you'll quickly notice how hard it is to connect shots with them.

Lowering your sensitivity is not a bad idea, but then you'll have to rely more on your radar and adjust your placement on the map so other players can't get the drop on you which the radar will help you with. I keep my sensitivity at the default setting but in your case it might be better to have it lower. If you notice you're getting better then slowly start increasing your sensitivity again. As a general rule always try to play defensive and never challenge more than one opponent at the same time. Playing like a coward rewards you the most in this game and doing it like that you'll notice your k/d will be much better as well.

Aim assist is a really weird stat in this game. It has its own sweetspot to activate on weapons depending on what range the weapon has and what weapon type it is.

But recently through my own testing I found (and this is anecdotal) that aim assist is tied to ping, but in  a reverse kind of way. My brother has his console down stairs and mine is in my room so when we go into a private match our ping is as low as can be since we're on the same network. This right here made it so that even if I aim at his legs at mid range it would often register as a crit. 

I then tested it with the hunter's new throwing knife and no matter what I did I just couldn't get a body shot with it. It was always a crit. Then I asked a friend from another continent to join up and tried the same tests and I immediately found out that there was way less aim assist with my spare rations and throwing knives.

Something  really funky is going on and I personally think that it's the developer's way of combatting bad connections since the game doesn't have dedicated servers. 

Anyways take this all with a grain of salt since I can't prove any of it aside from my own tests.

I don't want to start this again but there is a common consensus that opening shot conflicts with anything that increases aim assist such as a targeting adjuster mod. It's because opening shot maxes out the aim assist for that first shot and things like targeting adjuster may or may not increase it past 100 aim assist but instead it resets the aim assist from zero. So don't wear helmet mods that increase its aim assist either and see how it works now.

Anyway you should've put an icarus mod on it to begin with which will give you pinpoint accuracy when in the air.
If you already have the opening shot, you don't really need the targeting adjuster anyway because the opening shot maxes out the aim assist stat.
Make sure to take those mods off if you use a weapon with opening shot along with the targeting adjuster. You'll start to notice you're hitting your shots again after that.

Yeah there is zero evidence for it but there is also zero evidence against it. All I know is that lots of people are missing shots they're not supposed to when opening shot is combined with aim assist increasing stuff. 

The problem is that we don't know exactly how much aim assist makes a difference because it can't be properly tested by anyone. Only the game developer knows.

1) There are plenty of videos out there from top tier players that miss their shots and are all wtf about it. Way more on consoles due to bloom and such but also on pc players.

2) I recently made a video showcasing how messed up aim assist is on a private match with my brother who happens to be on the same home network and it turned out that in a low ping environment there is way more aim assist. So yeah tried it with a friend who lives on another continent and there was much less aim assist. 

The problem is definitely with the game's mechanics and netcode. This game can never be considered competitive when every engagement is basically a roll of the dice on who gets better hit registration unless there are some kind of dedicated servers.
